clue.text: A hospital return is all but necessity for this complaint

indicators.note: return means the hospital's name is read backwards, from last letter to first

parts.note: Bart's, St Bartholomew's in London, is a famous hospital
taken as written

indicators.note: all but means every letter except the last is kept

parts.note: a necessity is a must

explanation.surface: A patient going back to hospital is all but essential for treating some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns BARTS (St Bartholomew's, a London hospital) into STRAB; 'all but' drops the T of MUST, leaving MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Strabismus, a squint, is an eye disorder, so it is a medical complaint.

clue.text: Social occasion where all enjoy pot?

definitions.text: Social occasion where all enjoy pot?

parts.words: Social occasion where all enjoy pot?
parts.note: the pot sounds like cannabis shared at a party, but it is the teapot everyone drinks from at an afternoon gathering

explanation.surface: A gathering where everyone smokes marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon gathering where guests share a pot of tea is exactly this kind of occasion.

clue.text: Factory has no place for worker.

indicators.note: has no means the abbreviation for place is removed from the factory word

parts.note: a factory is a plant

explanation.surface: A factory with no room left for its workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker ant is the sterile labouring member of a colony, so crosswords use 'worker' for this insect.

clue.text: Pattern I had to recall on a regular basis

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

indicators.note: on a regular basis means every second letter of the word recall is taken

explanation.surface: A design I had to remember regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'recall', E, A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern in the sense of a perfect model to imitate is an ideal.

clue.text: In piece of Jewish ritual, wives put up with no interference

indicators.note: interference means the word no interferes by coming inside the other piece
in a down clue put up means the piece is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a harem is a group of wives
taken as written

explanation.surface: During a Jewish ceremony, wives tolerate no meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put up' means read upwards, giving MERAH; 'interference' looks like surface noise but signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The menorah is the seven-branched candelabrum used in Jewish worship, a ritual object.

clue.text: Drink, a long time — about a month — it puts an end to a starry career

definitions.text: it puts an end to a starry career

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: about means the long period goes round the month

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
NOV is the abbreviation for November

explanation.surface: A celebrity's drinking binge, lasting a month, ends their stellar career.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'about a month' look like a duration aside, but 'about' is a container signal wrapping the month inside the long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star's explosive death, the end of its life as a star.

clue.text: Fish, as fisherman's successor

definitions.meaning: a small freshwater fish, also called the ruffe
the head of the Roman Catholic Church succeeds St Peter, who was a fisherman

explanation.surface: A fish, as an angler's heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Popes are held to succeed St Peter, the fisherman apostle; the ruffe is also called this.

clue.text: Box with a white spot

parts.note: the box is not a container but the marked zone on a football pitch, with its painted spot for spot-kicks

explanation.surface: A box marked with a white dot.
explanation.walkthrough: In football the penalty area is known as 'the box', and the penalty spot is a painted white mark inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football pitch the zone called the box contains the white mark from which spot-kicks are taken.

clue.text: Professional woman perhaps a stunner

definitions.meaning: a member of the clergy, and women can now be ordained
a small club used by anglers to kill a landed fish is also called by this name

explanation.surface: A career woman who might be a knockout beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' looks like a beautiful woman, but it is the angler's club for stunning fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are professionals and may be women; anglers call their fish-stunning club by the same name.

clue.text: Cat runs off, working round temple

indicators.note: off means the runs abbreviation is taken away from the cat

parts.note: a panther is a big cat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A cat runs off while working around a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a containment instruction, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a famous circular temple with a domed roof.

clue.text: Chimp, say, I'd found by smell

indicators.note: found by means the I'd piece is placed beside the smell

parts.note: a pong is a bad smell
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: I'd tracked down a chimpanzee by its odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pongid is a member of the great-ape family, which includes chimpanzees.

clue.text: Permitted length's shocking

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for length
shocking means awful

explanation.surface: The allowed length is appalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted is legal, allowed under the law.

clue.text: Nothing libellous in criticism of exhibition

definitions.text: Nothing libellous in criticism of exhibition

parts.words: Nothing libellous in criticism of exhibition
parts.note: read as a remark about a fair (an exhibition), it is also the legal defence for honest opinion that is not defamatory

explanation.surface: A review of a show contains nothing defamatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one way it is a remark about a fair; in English law it is the defence that honest opinion on a public matter is not libel.
explanation.definitionFit: In law honest opinion on a matter of public interest is a defence against libel, so such criticism is not defamatory.

clue.text: Play a record for one that likes the Pastoral

parts.note: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's play that introduced the word robot
taken as written
a list is a record

explanation.surface: Putting on a record for a fan of Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Pastoral' suggests Beethoven's Sixth Symphony, but here it means the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruralist favours country life, the pastoral world.

clue.text: Explanation of matter's origin that has physicists tied in knots?

definitions.text: Explanation of matter's origin that has physicists tied in knots?

parts.words: Explanation of matter's origin that has physicists tied in knots?
parts.note: a model of fundamental particles as tiny vibrating strands, joking that these strands get tied in knots and so do the scientists

explanation.surface: A cosmological theory that leaves physicists baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: This physics framework models fundamental particles as vibrating one-dimensional strands.

clue.text: Very agile, succeeded in developing my minute, acting

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Very agile, succeeded in developing my minute, acting (9)': S in an anagram of MY ACTING gives the answer, leaving 'minute' with no job (M would be one letter too many); the scan is blank and no source gives the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Very agile, succeeded in developing my minute, acting

clue.text: Offhand, I'd say Herrick and Lovelace were such poets

definitions.text: Herrick and Lovelace were such poets
definitions.meaning: Robert Herrick and Richard Lovelace were 17th-century Royalist lyric poets

explanation.surface: Casually, I'd suggest these two poets belonged to one school.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand; the Cavalier poets were Royalist lyricists of Charles I's court.

clue.text: Join free outing and perk up a lot

parts.note: to come on is to join, as a player joins a game
a treat is an outing someone else pays for

explanation.surface: Sign up for a complimentary trip and cheer up considerably.
explanation.definitionFit: To come on a treat is an informal British idiom for improving greatly.

clue.text: Elements of date in wrong order, part omitted from broadcast

indicators.note: elements of says the date phrase comes in separate parts to be handled
in wrong order means the two parts of the phrase swap places

parts.note: to date someone is to take them out

explanation.surface: Parts of a calendar date jumbled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' is the phrase TAKE OUT; 'Elements of' and 'in wrong order' swap its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An outtake is a scene cut from a film or broadcast before it airs.

clue.text: Well-behaved author's on fire inside

indicators.note: inside means the burning word sits within the author's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe is an author
something lit is on fire

explanation.surface: A well-mannered writer has a burning passion within.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite and well-behaved both describe courteous, mannerly conduct.

clue.text: Computer infection found — a groundbreaking result, in a small way

definitions.text: a groundbreaking result, in a small way

parts.note: a worm is a self-spreading computer virus
to found metal is to cast it

explanation.surface: A computer virus discovered, which proves a groundbreaking finding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' means cast, as in a foundry, not discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm cast is the little coil of soil an earthworm leaves where it breaks the ground surface.

clue.text: Menswear involves a tax, when got on credit

indicators.note: got on means the credit abbreviation goes on top of, that is before, the rest

parts.note: taken as written
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A man's neckwear comes with sales tax when bought on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a man's neckscarf, an item of men's clothing.

clue.text: Manage with spades inside wood

indicators.note: inside means the spades abbreviation goes within the other word

parts.note: to cope is to manage
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Getting by with shovels in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood or thicket of trees.

clue.text: Fateful court order

parts.note: dire means dreadful or ominous, fateful

explanation.surface: A judge's decisive ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court order' looks like one legal phrase; the definition is 'order' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to order or instruct them.

clue.text: Final part of work often discarded in theatre

definitions.meaning: supplementary matter at the end of a book
the small organ often removed in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: The closing section of a play, which often gets cut in performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests a stage, but it is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's back matter and the vestigial organ surgeons remove share this name.

clue.text: Butt's keen admirer

definitions.meaning: to butt is to strike with the head
an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a sports fanatic

explanation.surface: A target's devoted fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for headbutting someone, and also for an enthusiast or fanatic.

clue.text: Considered material

definitions.meaning: believed or judged, as in a view one held

explanation.surface: Fabric that has been thought about.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of feel means considered; a pressed wool fabric has the same name.

clue.text: Part of church secretly dug up, and gold buried

indicators.note: buried means the gold sits within the rearranged letters
dug up means the letters of secretly are turned over into a new order

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Treasure secretly excavated from a church, where gold had been hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secretly' looks like an adverb on 'dug up', but it is the anagram fodder, giving CLERESTY; 'buried' tucks the heraldic gold in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The clerestory is the upper wall of a church nave, pierced with windows.
